AS A RESULT OF THE COVID-19 VIRUS, AND RESULTING ORDERS AND DIRECTION FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, THE GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AND THE ORANGE COUNTY HEALTH CARE AGENCY, AS WELL AS THE CITY OF IRVINE EMERGENCY DECLARATION, THE PUBLIC WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO PHYSICALLY ATTEND THE IRVINE CITY COUNCIL MEETING TO WHICH THIS AGENDA APPLIES.
YOU MAY SUBMIT COMMENTS ON ANY AGENDA ITEM OR ON ANY ITEM NOT ON THE AGENDA, IN WRITING VIA MAIL TO “ATTN: CITY COUNCIL,” ONE CIVIC CENTER PLAZA, IRVINE, CA 92606; BY EMAIL TO CLERK@CITYOFIRVINE.ORG; OR THROUGH E-COMMENT AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. YOU MAY WATCH THE MEETING LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV.
PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. IT WOULD BE APPRECIATED IF COMMUNICATIONS OF PUBLIC COMMENTS RELATED TO ITEMS ON THE AGENDA, OR ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA, ARE PROVIDED PRIOR TO THE COMMENCEMENT OF THE MEETING. IF THAT IS NOT POSSIBLE, EVERY EFFORT WILL BE MADE TO ATTEMPT TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS DURING THE COURSE OF THE MEETING. TOWARDS THIS END, THE MAYOR WILL ENDEAVOR TO TAKE A BRIEF PAUSE BEFORE ACTION IS TAKEN ON ANY AGENDA ITEM TO ALLOW THE CITY CLERK TO REVIEW E-COMMENTS, AND SHARE ANY E-COMMENTS RECEIVED DURING THE MEETING.

LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  November 10, 2020
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, OA 92606

CALL TO ORDER

The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:06 p.m. on
November 10, 2020, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center
Plaza, Irvine, Califomia; Mayor Shea presiding.

ROLL CALL

  Present:  Councilmember  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember  Farrah N. Khan
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Mike Carroll
  Mayor  Christina Shea

Mayor Shea announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox Communications
Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and livestreamed online at
cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and prevent the spread of
COVID-19, the e-comment feature had been extended for all agenda items, which
allowed members of the public the ability to submit e-comments through the public
comment portion of each item and would be included as part of the official record and
uploaded to the City's website. She also assured the community that the City of Irvine
was adhering to the Governor's Executive Order in the Council Chamber and throughout
City Hall by sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.

Mayor Shea also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m., which had been
standard practice prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, and expressed her appreciation for
everyone's patience and understanding as the City continued to make adjustments to
meeting protocols as needed.
 City Council Minutes  November 10. 2020

  Mayor Shea further noted that following the Pledge of Allegiance and Invocation, Vice
  Mayor Carroll would be presiding over the meeting as she would be participating in a
  required conference call.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Khan led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Councilmember Kuo provided the invocation.

  Mayor Shea left the dais at 4:55 p.m. Vice Mayor Carroll assumed the role of presiding
  officer during her absence.

  PRESENTATIONS

  1.1  Silverado Fire Update and Adoption of a Resolution Declaring
  Termination of the Silverado Fire Emergency

  Mike Hamel, Director of Public Safety/Chief of Police, Shane Sherwood,
  Orange County Fire Authority Division Chief, and Casey Gnadt, Open
  Space Administrator, provided an update on the Silverado Fire and
  responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: noting the successfulness of the
  evacuation through multi-agency cooperation; expressed appreciation
  for efficient and timely updates provided during the fires; inquired about
  how residents could assist with landscaping lost due to the fire; and
  expressed condolences to the firefighters injured during the fire.

  Carl Petersen, Assistant City Clerk, noted that the following e-comments
  had been received:

  • Emily Liu, who expressed concern about All American Asphalt and
  suggested the City return to holistic grazing.

  • Cherry Lai, who expressed appreciation to the Orange County Fire
  Authority and Irvine Police Department, and noted confusion with
  the evacuation map.

  • Jonathan Beer, who expressed concern about climate change and
  suggested the City have a robust plan in place for the future.

  Prepared by the City Clerk's Office
 City Council Minutes  November 10. 2020

  ACTION:  Moved  by  Councllmember  Kuo,  seconded  by
  Councilmember Khan, to:

  Adopt RESOLUTION NO. 20-87 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, TERMINATING
  THE LOCAL EMERGENCY RESULTING FROM THE SILVERADO
  WILDFIRE

  The motion carried as follows:

  AYES:  4  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Carroll, Fox, Khan and
  Kuo

  NOES:  0  COUNCILMEMBERS:  None

  ABSENT:  1  COUNCILMEMBERS:  Shea

  1.2  Community Choice Energy Update

  Mark Steuer, Director of Public Works and Transportation, Ryan Baron,
  Best Best and Krieger, and Gary Saleba, EES Consulting, provided the
  update and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: inquiring about concerns raised by
  other cities: questioned the difference in governance related to two board
  seats and the alternative weighted vote options; expressed concern
  about liabilities and associated impacts to Irvine; inquired about the
  source of the $2.5 million loan and related terms; requested clarity on the
  member withdrawal process; expressed concern about the potential lack
  of financial investments from other participating cities; and questioned
  next steps to move forward with the Joint Powers Authority (JPA)
  Agreement.

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, clarified deal points included in the JPA
  agreement.

  ACTION:  Moved  by  Councilmember  Khan, seconded  by
  Councilmember Fox, to:

  1) Direct staff to complete negotiations with other participating
  cities and approve the JPA Agreement including the following
  modifications:

  A capital loan of $250,000 in the first tranche, up to $2.5
  million for start-up costs, and collateral for the power
  purchase loan with an eight(8) year contemplated term.
  Governance: Two(2)votes for the City of Irvine until the
  capital loan is repaid, and the alternative weighted vote
  would continue on in perpetuity.
  No penalty for exit prior to March 2021
  Clarity on the member withdrawal process
  Four year term of office
  An Executive Committee of Founding Members
  Meetings can occur with a quorum
  Special voting does not require affirmative vote of Irvine
  directors
  A Statement regarding ratepayer equity

  2) Provide City staff and outside counsel the authority to make
  such other modifications that are consistent with City Council
  direction.
  3) Grant authority to the City Manager to sign the agreement once
  fully approved.

 City Council Minutes  November 10. 2020

  Mayor Shea made the following announcements:

  • The City of Irvine will be hosting a special modified Veterans Day Ceremony on
  Wednesday, November 11, to pay tribute to our nation's troops, past and present,
  and honor local veterans, veterans groups, and military organizations. The
  traditional Veterans Day ceremony will be presented online at cityofirvine.org for
  the community to view at their convenience. A prerecorded video presentation by
  the Mayor will include remarks from officers from the adopted 2/11 Marine
  Battalion, and musical performances and event footage from past ceremonies. For
  more information, visit cityofirvine.org/specialevents or call 949-724-6606.

  • Join the City of Irvine and the Irvine 2/11 Marine Adoption Committee in brightening
  the season for military families by participating in the annual Holiday Toy Drive
  underway now through December 14. This community effort supports the families
  of Irvine's adopted 2/11 Marine Battalion by donating an unwrapped gift suitable
  for an infant or child age 12 or younger. Donation bins are located at City Hall, the
  Irvine Police Department, and the Orange County Great Park Visitors Center. In
  addition, there will be two drive-thru, drop-off events Saturday, December 5 and
  Saturday, December 12 from 9 a.m. to noon at the Irvine Civic Center. Monetary
  donations and donations through AmazonSmile are also being accepted. To
  donate online and for more information, visit cityofirvine.org/211.

  • Santa is going digital this holiday season, and would love to hear from his friends.
  Beginning Monday, November 16, children can email their letters to Santa. To
  keep Santa and his elves safe this year, in-person drop-off and pick-up will not be
  available. All letters will receive email responses a week after they are received.
  Classrooms should allow two weeks for responses. For more information, including
  Santa's email address, visit cityofirvine.org.

  • A virtual holiday celebration with all City Councilmembers will be held on
  December 1.
